recipes.name: Brandied Candied Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds sweet potatoes, peeled and diced

steps.text: Place sweet potatoes in a large saucepan with enough water to cover. Bring to a boil. Cook 15 minutes, or until tender but firm. Drain and set aside.

In a large skillet over low heat, melt butter. Stir in brown sugar, brandy, and salt. Add sweet potatoes and stir to coat. Cook, stirring gently until sweet potatoes are heated through and thoroughly glazed.

raw_recipe.headline: Brandied Candied Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These brandied, candied sweet potatoes have been a Thanksgiving favorite of ours for many years because they are different from the many mashed sweet potato recipes.

review.reviewBody: This recipe has been updated to include a step for boiling the sweet potatoes, as per the original submission.

This is a quick & easy side to put together. My substitutions were 2 tbsp butter & 2 tbsp coconut oil (for 1/2 cup butter) and 1/2 cup coconut sugar (for 1/2 cup brown sugar)...and I chose to steam my peeled, cubed sweet potatoes instead of boil them. Tender, flavorful...delicious!!

Hubby really, really liked these. I simmered the butter and brandy for about 8 minutes on low before adding brown sugar to give it a smooth/non-alcohol flavor!... Very good! Also topped with pecans and a few miniature marshmallows. Picture was before I browned them at Moms on Thanksgiving! I use yams instead of sweet potatoes because of the bright pretty color... The taste and texture is the same!

I had to make this twice. Maybe I added the potatoes too soon but the glaze became so watery it turned the potatoes to mush by the time it thickened. I only had one 1lb sweet potato left, so I cut the ingredients in half and started over and it turned out perfect. The Brandy flavor really carries through and both tasted great. Nice recipe I'll figure out what went wrong next batch.

I ended up adding about 1/4 cup more brown sugar and a handful of walnuts; baked at 350 degrees for 30 minutes and added mini marshmallows, returned to oven to 'tan' the mallows. Very good and we did not think the brandy was over whelming.

My husband couldn't stop raving about these sweet potatoes. I thought the alcohol taste was a little overwhelming & I would suggest reducing the sauce down to be more like a glaze before adding the potatoes. Very easy. Will continue to make it for husband but will try cutting back on the brandy next time.

I made these along with my traditional candied yams, they were DELISH. I actually made them wednesday night and put them in an 8x8 pan and baked them about 20 prior to turkey time and they caramelized a bit more.
Actually first time adding brandy.. I used BlackBerry! Delicious 😋

Absoulutely delicious!! I used brandy and sherry and it was perfect. My dish DID incorporate the sauce, I cooked it as suggested but turned it or flipped it and let it cook another few minutes so it was well done and tender and had a nice crust at the edges. Will make it again and again especially for company.
These are YAMS, not Sweet Potatoes. Sweet Potatoes are off-white and do not have the flavor of YAMS. I add pecans and some cranberries for flavor and color.

I was worried cause so many people thought this recipe had too much booze taste. I am not a big drinker, but I didnt taste the brandy at all. Purely delicious potatoes! Easy too! Beat the pants off whipped sweet potatoes for Thanksgiving. I cooked themin advance and put them in a casserole to reheat. For traditions sake, I melted a few miniature marmallows on top. Everybody raved!
my mom always made sweet potatoes with brandy in it Delicious l'm going to make this year

So so good! And, even better as leftovers! Don’t be afraid of the brandy. Can’t taste it at all. It is a little sweet overall. So, if you don’t like sweet you may not like it. But, I found it DELICIOUS!

Well, to start with I over cooked the sweet potatoes. They looked like they might hold together and of course they did not! What the hey, I'll just go for it. I had the other ingredients except for the brandy. The two choices I had were tequila and Irish whiskey and to stick with my mothers heritage I chose the whiskey. No mistake there as the largest part of the gathering was raving about the taste of the dish . Thanks for printing the recipe and giving an old man a chance for some compliments!
I love this recipe. Very easy to make and it is delicious. I added chopped pecans. I am always going to keep some brandy in my kitchen from now on.!
I first made this for Thanksgiving about five years ago, and I loved it so much I've made it every year since!
Sooooo good!!
Excellent for Christmas. I took suggestions and put them in oven! A true hit!
It tasted great. I will try it again.
Its a keeper. Great flavor.
